problem_found: Locations in the Bengaluru box are a mix of reference monitors, low-cost sensors and locations without PM2.5
action_taken: Kept only fixed reference monitors with a PM2.5 sensor
why: Low-cost and mobile sensors measure differently; mixing them compares unlike things

problem_found: Stations list several PM2.5 sensor ids; old ids have no data in our range (OpenAQ re-issued sensor ids)
action_taken: Treat all ids of one location as one station; per day take the id that reported
why: Otherwise one station would look like two, one of them empty

problem_found: Monitors below 60% PM2.5 coverage for the study range
action_taken: Dropped; kept 7 stations with coverage >= 60%
why: Too few complete evenings to time the evening peak; 70% left only 5 stations, so the team chose 60% (M5)

problem_found: Approved stations also list sensor ids for our pollutants whose last reading is before 2025-10-01
action_taken: Skipped these old ids when downloading
why: They only return empty pages; the station's new id carries the data

problem_found: OpenAQ hourly records are nested JSON (32 columns after json_normalize: parameter, period, summary, coverage objects)
action_taken: Flattened with pd.json_normalize; kept 8 columns + station/sensor ids
why: Tables and SQL need one value per cell; summary quantiles are not used in our question

problem_found: Open-Meteo sends parallel arrays (time[], rain[], ...) instead of records
action_taken: Turned each array into a column with pd.DataFrame
why: Different JSON shape from OpenAQ; both must end up as one row per hour

problem_found: OpenAQ timestamps are ISO-8601 text in UTC ('...Z'), plus a second local copy with a '+05:30' offset
action_taken: Parsed UTC with pd.to_datetime(utc=True) and converted to IST (Asia/Kolkata); 0 unparseable
why: MySQL and our charts need one clock; the commissioner thinks in IST

problem_found: Need proof that our UTC->IST conversion is right
action_taken: Compared our IST with OpenAQ's own '+05:30' local time; rows_affected = mismatches
why: An independent check: 0 mismatches means the conversion is correct

problem_found: OpenAQ hours start at :30 UTC, i.e. on the hour in IST
action_taken: Checked every ts_ist falls on :00 IST; rows_affected = rows that do not
why: Confirms each reading is the average for the IST hour starting at ts_ist

problem_found: Values must be numbers; text values would break averages
action_taken: pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce') then float64; rows_affected = text values turned missing
why: OpenAQ JSON already sends numbers (33 were null on arrival); the cast guards against text from CPCB files if we add them

problem_found: NO2 arrives in ppb, but Indian AQI breakpoints use µg/m³
action_taken: Converted: value x 1.88162 (MW 46.0055 / 24.45, at 25 C, 1 atm)
why: Same units as the CPCB AQI table; 25 C/1 atm is the standard reference condition

problem_found: CO arrives in ppb, but Indian AQI breakpoints use mg/m³
action_taken: Converted: value x 0.00115 (MW 28.01 / 24.45 / 1000, at 25 C, 1 atm)
why: Same units as the CPCB AQI table; 25 C/1 atm is the standard reference condition

problem_found: Same station, parameter and IST hour appears more than once (0 rows involved; month-boundary hours or overlapping sensor ids)
action_taken: Kept one row per key, preferring the higher observed_count
why: A duplicate would count that hour twice in every average

problem_found: Open-Meteo times are text with NO zone ('2025-10-01T00:00'); GMT because we requested timezone=GMT
action_taken: Parsed, labelled as UTC (tz_localize), converted to IST (tz_convert)
why: Doing the conversion ourselves makes it visible and checkable, not hidden in the API

problem_found: Weather hours start at :30 IST; air-quality hours start at :00 IST
action_taken: Instantaneous vars: value at the half-hour label (= middle of the IST hour). Rain: average of the two overlapping hourly totals x 2 halves; 1 edge hour(s) left missing
why: Joining on the raw labels would match every air reading with weather 30 minutes off

problem_found: Need a yes/no rain flag per hour
action_taken: is_rain_hour = precip_mm >= 0.1; rows_affected = rain hours
why: 0.1 mm is the smallest measurable rainfall on a standard rain gauge

problem_found: Sanity check of the IST conversion
action_taken: Mean NO2 by IST hour peaks at 7:00 (morning) and 19:00 (evening); saved outputs/tables/ist_sanity_check.csv
why: Traffic NO2 should peak in the rush hours; plausible IST peaks support the conversion

problem_found: Hours the API never sent, after building the full hourly grid (279,552 station-parameter-hours)
action_taken: Counted per station and parameter (outputs/tables/gaps_per_station.csv)
why: Gaps must be visible before any rule touches them; silent dropping hides bias

problem_found: Longest PM2.5 gap: 1491 hours (~62 days) at BLR5607
action_taken: Not filled (far beyond the 3-hour limit); those evenings drop out of peak timing
why: Inventing days of data would be fabrication

problem_found: Sensor error codes 999 / 9999
action_taken: qc_flag = 'sentinel'; value blanked (treated as a gap)
why: Loggers write these when the analyser fails; not air

problem_found: Values above the analyser's measuring range
action_taken: qc_flag = 'out_of_range'; value blanked (treated as a gap)
why: Physically not measurable; an error code

problem_found: Negative concentrations
action_taken: qc_flag = 'negative'; value blanked (treated as a gap)
why: A concentration cannot be below zero; usually a calibration drift

problem_found: Exact zero readings
action_taken: qc_flag = 'zero'; value blanked (treated as a gap)
why: Bengaluru city air is never exactly zero for these pollutants

problem_found: Flat-lines: same value repeated for >= 6 hours (CO >= 12)
action_taken: qc_flag = 'flatline'; value blanked (treated as a gap)
why: A working sensor jitters; an exact repeat for hours means it is stuck

problem_found: Single-hour spikes (> 5x both neighbours and a large jump) NOT on a festival night or in heavy rain
action_taken: qc_flag = 'spike'; value blanked
why: Real pollution builds and fades over hours; one isolated hour that jumps and drops back is a glitch

problem_found: Extreme values (above each station's 99.5th percentile): real_event_festival
action_taken: Kept; qc_flag = 'real_event_festival'
why: Fireworks on festival nights (e.g. Deepavali) are real pollution

problem_found: Extreme values (above each station's 99.5th percentile): real_event_rain
action_taken: Kept; qc_flag = 'real_event_rain'
why: Extreme values during >= 10 mm/h rain: real weather, kept for the event study

problem_found: Extreme values (above each station's 99.5th percentile): real_event_citywide
action_taken: Kept; qc_flag = 'real_event_citywide'
why: >= 3 stations extreme in the same hour: the air itself, not one sensor

problem_found: Extreme values (above each station's 99.5th percentile): extreme_unexplained
action_taken: Kept; qc_flag = 'extreme_unexplained'
why: Above the 99.5th percentile, no festival/rain/city-wide match: kept but sent to manual review (M11)

problem_found: Manual review (M11) of 10 flagged PM2.5 hours: verdict applied to the whole high-value episode around each
action_taken: Episodes judged sensor failures: qc_flag = 'failure_reviewed', value blanked
why: A human looked at build-up, other stations, rain and festivals (see report/reflection_notes.md)

problem_found: Manual review (M11): episodes judged real events
action_taken: qc_flag = 'real_event_reviewed'; kept
why: Real extreme air must stay in the data, or we would understate the worst evenings

problem_found: Short gaps (<= 3 consecutive hours) in pollutant series
action_taken: Forward-filled, limit 3 hours; is_filled = True on every filled value
why: Keeps hourly averages from losing whole hours to brief dropouts, without inventing long stretches

problem_found: Gaps longer than 3 hours
action_taken: Left missing (not filled)
why: Beyond 3 hours we would be guessing

problem_found: Station-evenings with fewer than 6 of 7 real PM2.5 hours (out of 2,912 station-evenings)
action_taken: Excluded from peak-timing analysis (evening_usable = False); kept for averages
why: With 2+ evening hours missing we cannot tell WHEN the peak happened

problem_found: Missing hours in smooth weather variables (temperature, humidity, wind, boundary layer)
action_taken: Linear interpolation, at most 3 hours
why: These change smoothly hour to hour, so a straight line is a fair estimate

problem_found: Missing rain hours
action_taken: Not filled
why: Rain starts and stops suddenly; interpolating would invent showers

problem_found: Rows with no usable value (never sent, or blanked as a sensor failure)
action_taken: Filtered out in Spark before aggregating
why: An empty or failed reading must not pull averages towards zero

problem_found: Joining PM2.5 hours to weather and calendar
action_taken: Left joins keep all 55,026 PM2.5 rows; rows_affected = rows that found no weather (0) or no calendar day (0)
why: A left join never silently drops air-quality hours; unmatched rows are counted
